inputs.title: The Thing
inputs.logline: When Bo’s big tail betrays how hard it is to meet new friends, Keen and Aida help him discover that the very thing he wants to hide may be the first thing everyone loves.

orderedEvents.text: Golden morning light. Dew sparkles on wildflowers. A honeycomb sits on a small stump. KEEN tiptoes toward it. He lifts his knees high with every step.
CRUNCH. CRUNCH. CRUNCH.
Keen freezes each time. He spots the honeycomb. His eyes widen. He LICKS HIS LIPS. He reaches toward the honey. FUZZBY the bee is asleep on top of the honeycomb.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
A small snore bubble grows from his nose. Keen reaches closer to the honey. POP! The bubble bursts. Keen FREEZES.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
Another bubble slowly grows. Keen inches closer to the honey.
POP! The second bubble bursts.

beats.storyBeat: Keen attempts an exaggerated stealth mission toward Fuzzby’s honeycomb, but every crunchy step and snore-bubble pop makes the world more awake than he wants it to be. The beat is about borrowed boldness meeting tiny physical resistance.
beats.want: Keen wants to get close enough to take honey without waking Fuzzby.
beats.need: He needs to learn that rushing toward what he wants is not the same as being ready or unseen.
beats.kidRead: Keen is being silly-sneaky and the sleeping bee might wake up any second.
beats.adultRead: A child’s confidence is charmingly exposed by his own body and the environment; he is not as invisible as he thinks.
beats.emotionalIntent: Light suspense and giggly anticipation, with the honeycomb as the forbidden prize.

beats.adultRead: The comedy is the impossibility of controlling every tell; Keen’s cover is doomed because he is still a kid in a too-big plan.
beats.emotionalIntent: Build the laugh through anticipation, release it with the sneeze, then button it with Fuzzby’s sleepy authority.

beats.need: She needs to trust the quiet signal and make room for someone else’s fear without taking over.
beats.kidRead: A magic bowl shows a squirrel who keeps packing but does not go anywhere.
beats.adultRead: The repetition is instantly recognizable as a child trying to make a hard transition feel controllable.
beats.emotionalIntent: Quiet wonder with a small ache under it; the vision should feel intimate, not flashy.

beats.storyBeat: Inside the hollow tree, Bo answers his offscreen Mum but bargains with time and his conker, delaying the Learning Circle by making “a minute” stretch absurdly. The safe room is cosy, but it is also a trap of postponement.
beats.want: Bo wants to put off leaving while sounding like he still intends to go.
beats.need: He needs to be witnessed in the stuck place instead of left alone with the loop.
beats.kidRead: Bo keeps finding reasons not to go yet, and his conker is like his little helper.
beats.adultRead: The offscreen parent call captures the morning-transition ache: encouragement from another room cannot cross the threshold for him.
beats.emotionalIntent: Tender comic avoidance; keep it small, domestic and recognisable.

vision.premise: Bo is due at the Learning Circle for the first time, but every step toward the door makes his tail poof with worry. Keen’s playful curiosity and Aida’s quiet truth help him move toward the group one step at a time, until the tail he feared becomes his way in.
vision.dramaticQuestion: Can Bo go to the Learning Circle without having to hide the part of himself that gives him away?
vision.theme: Belonging begins when the thing you were trying to hide is gently witnessed and welcomed.
vision.externalJourney: Keen fails to steal honey, is redirected by Aida, visits Bo’s hollow tree, walks him through the woods, helps him arrive at the Learning Circle, and returns home to find Fuzzby attempting his own honey heist.
vision.internalJourney: Bo moves from delaying and controlling every detail to taking a visible step forward with his worry still present, then letting his tail become play instead of proof that something is wrong with him.
vision.relationshipChanges: Bo and Keen shift from strangers at a doorway to easy friends; Bo and Aida move from cautious distance to shared truth; Bo and the Learning Circle group move from imagined judgement to delighted acceptance. Fuzzby and Zenny provide the comic echo: being ridiculous and still belonging.
vision.emotionalCurve: Playful mischief opens the episode, then narrows into Bo’s held-at-the-door worry. The woods give relief through play, dip again at the log, soften through Aida’s honesty, glow into the walk forward, burst into group joy, and settle in a warm, lightly comic garden coda.
vision.comedyCurve: The comedy starts with stealth, snore bubbles, pollen and sneezes; turns into tail-poof escalation and Keen’s useless-tail demonstration; blooms into group delight at the Learning Circle; and ends with Fuzzby’s flower-disguise failure and Zenny’s tiny crack of amusement.
vision.setupPayoffMap: The untouched honeycomb and Fuzzby’s “never ever” return in the final garden heist. Bo’s conker and repeated packing plant his need for control. The tail’s first unwanted poof pays off as a chosen game in the woods and then as the Learning Circle’s delight. Aida’s vision of Bo unable to move pays off in Bo walking forward under pink and blue light. “Every single time” moves from Aida’s truth to Bo’s own action phrase.
vision.visualMotifs: Closed/open thresholds, paws holding objects too tightly, Bo’s tail expanding beyond his control, the forest path as a visible line between home and belonging, and the honeycomb as comic temptation that remains untouched.
vision.sonicMotifs: Crunching steps, snore-bubble pops, sneeze blasts, the shave-and-a-haircut knock, tail POOFs, Aida’s bowl tone, rose and aquamarine glow tones, group cheers, and Zenny’s bookend Ommmm.
vision.climax: Aida and Keen each offer their crystal truth, pink and blue light join on the forest path, and Bo takes one step, then another, toward the Learning Circle.
vision.resolution: At the Learning Circle, Bo’s tail poofs in front of everyone and is met with wonder, cheering and play; later, he draws with Keen while Aida watches his settled belonging from the edge of the clearing.
vision.intendedFinalFeeling: Warm, giggly relief: the child feels the fun of the fluffy tail, while the adult feels the ache of a child being welcomed without needing to edit himself.

northStar.surfaceStory: Keen turns Bo’s tail poof into a countdown game on the forest path; the fun pauses when Bo remembers he still has to meet the Learning Circle, and Aida joins him with comic humility and a quiet truth: she gets scared and still goes.
northStar.universalTruth: A first step can feel easier when someone proves you do not have to stop being scared before you take it.

northStar.emotionalNeed: Bo needs to feel witnessed beside his worry, not rushed past it or fixed out of it.

northStar.ordinaryLifeTruth: Children can briefly turn embarrassment into a joke, but the real fear returns when the room of people becomes real; what helps is not a speech, but someone safe admitting they feel it too.

orderedEvents.text: Golden morning light. Dew sparkles on wildflowers. A honeycomb sits on a small stump. KEEN tiptoes toward it. He lifts his knees high with every step.
CRUNCH. CRUNCH. CRUNCH.
Keen freezes each time. He spots the honeycomb. His eyes widen. He LICKS HIS LIPS. He reaches toward the honey. FUZZBY the bee is asleep on top of the honeycomb.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
A small snore bubble grows from his nose. Keen reaches closer to the honey. POP! The bubble bursts. Keen FREEZES.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
Another bubble slowly grows. Keen inches closer to the honey.
POP! The second bubble bursts.

beats.storyBeat: Keen attempts an exaggerated stealth mission toward Fuzzby’s honeycomb, but every crunchy step and snore-bubble pop makes the world more awake than he wants it to be. The beat is about borrowed boldness meeting tiny physical resistance.
beats.want: Keen wants to get close enough to take honey without waking Fuzzby.
beats.need: He needs to learn that rushing toward what he wants is not the same as being ready or unseen.
beats.kidRead: Keen is being silly-sneaky and the sleeping bee might wake up any second.
beats.adultRead: A child’s confidence is charmingly exposed by his own body and the environment; he is not as invisible as he thinks.
beats.emotionalIntent: Light suspense and giggly anticipation, with the honeycomb as the forbidden prize.

treatments.name: Countdown That Runs Out of Road
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience starts inside a giggly game: the tail is a prize that keeps paying off on command. The suspense is not danger; it is the child's delight of “again!” Then the same rhythm runs out of bounce when Bo remembers the Learning Circle. The scene should feel like a laugh that gently becomes a held breath, then lands in quiet courage without pretending the worry has vanished.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: Bo governs the emotional experience. Keen’s countdown gives him a few seconds of ownership over the thing that embarrassed him, but the path ahead keeps tugging at the worry underneath. Aida’s arrival does not replace Bo’s point of view; it answers it by proving that steadiness can arrive with twigs in it.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Primary comic mechanism: repetition with emotional reversal. “3,2,1 … POOF!” is funny because Bo can trigger the result again and again, and each successful poof briefly re-titles the tail from problem to trick. Dramatic mechanism: the game’s countdown becomes a countdown toward the thing Bo is avoiding. When the rhythm stops, the absence of the game is the turn.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Keen performs support as play first: bright, forward, invested in making the tail feel like a shared invention instead of an exposed flaw. When Bo says the worry, Keen’s support changes physically; he lowers beside Bo rather than pulling him onward. Bo begins with delighted participation, giggling through small bursts of pride, then his body loses its spring as the Learning Circle becomes real again. He does not hide the tail at the end; the courage is that it remains visible. Aida enters with earned humility: she is still grounded and warm, but the twigs and leaf make her first impression gently human before she offers reassurance. Her “Every single time” is not a grand lesson; it is a plain truth she has carried often.
treatments.visualGrammar: The visual grammar begins in rhythmic bursts: dappled light, little pockets of motion, tail poofs that briefly fill the frame’s attention. As Bo’s worry returns, the grammar settles lower and wider around bodies sitting near the path. By Aida’s final answer, the frame has stopped chasing the poof and is listening to breath, leaves and stillness.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera is Bo-adjacent: close enough to feel the pleasure of making the tail respond, then close enough to feel the drop when his attention leaves the game and finds the path. It can be surprised by the poof early, then become patient once Bo speaks the worry. With Aida, the camera does not crown her from a safe distance; it discovers her imperfect descent with the same affectionate honesty Bo does.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Movement belongs to the game: Keen’s countdown energy, Bo’s repeated poof, little recoils of delight. Stillness arrives as care: Keen sitting beside Bo, Aida making space, Bo listening. The scene’s emotional construction depends on the contrast between playful popping and three characters choosing not to rush the next step.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: The forest path is never neutral. In the game portion, it is a play lane sprinkled with sunlight. In the worry portion, it becomes a visible route toward offscreen others. The trees carry soft wind after Aida’s final line, reminding us the Learning Circle still exists beyond the frame. Aida’s messy arrival uses the ridge and trees as gentle participants rather than obstacles with blame.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: Start with repeatable comic rhythm: countdown, poof, giggle, again. Escalate not by getting louder, but by making the repetition feel briefly mastered. Then break the pattern with Bo’s worry. The middle slows into honest pauses: Bo names the social fear, Keen sits, Aida arrives imperfectly, the bag exchange lets comedy breathe. The final escalation is inward: Bo’s questions get smaller and more direct; Aida’s repeated answer lands heavier the second time.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts are motivated by changed emotional ownership, not by coverage. Early cuts may punctuate the poof rhythm and surprise. Once Bo says the worry, fewer cuts; the frame should earn its stay while the characters make space. Aida’s entrance can justify a fresh visual idea because her arrival changes the room. The final BEAT after “Every single time.” should not be cut away from too quickly; the wind and visible tail need time to carry the cost.
treatments.openingImage: A sun-dappled tail poof blooms on command at forest-path height while Keen’s countdown energy hangs in the air, turning an embarrassment into a tiny celebration before we have settled into any safe master view.
treatments.closingImage: Bo, Keen and Aida sit in a quiet cluster beside the path. Bo’s tail remains visible in the open, no longer performing for laughs and not tucked away. Beyond them, the path continues under moving leaves.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: Do not make this a tidy dialogue triangle after the game stops. The risk is safe, static blocking: Bo speaks, Keen reacts, Aida advises. I challenge us to let the camera’s grammar visibly change from popping play to seated listening, and to let the path occupy emotional space without resorting to a re-establishing wide.

treatments.name: The Path Watches Back
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience feels the forest path as a gentle invitation that Bo keeps turning into a playground. The child reads a funny countdown game; the adult feels how play can postpone a doorway moment. When Bo finally says the worry, the path seems to grow longer without becoming scary. The ending leaves viewers with the sense that the next step is still there, but Bo is no longer standing in front of it by himself.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: The governing point of view is the path’s pressure on Bo. We experience Bo from just outside his private bubble, as though the forest itself is patiently waiting for him to come along. Keen and Aida are not there to solve the path; they change how it feels to stand beside it.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Primary comic mechanism: environmental participation. The tail poofs disturb little bits of the path world — dust, dappled leaves, tiny drifting fluff — so the forest joins the game. Aida’s “Tricky trees.” continues the same mechanism: the environment has touched her too. Dramatic mechanism: the environment stops playing along for a moment, and the wind through the trees replaces the countdown as the scene’s rhythm.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Bo treats the poof as proof that he can manage what gives him away. He leans into the game with real giggles, then turns quieter when the path ahead becomes other bears who already know each other. Keen is not a coach pushing progress; he is a playmate who knows when to sit down. His change of level is the support. Aida’s performance is warm and unembarrassed by imperfection: the twigs and leaf do not make her silly in her own eyes, which is exactly why Bo can trust her. Her repetitions are steady, small and unforced.
treatments.visualGrammar: Frames should give the path agency. Early, the composition can let the countdown and poof happen against a path that curves forward, keeping the destination present even during the joke. The forest is dimensional and alive: foreground grasses, middle-ground characters, background bend of path and trees. As the scene quiets, the depth becomes emotional rather than decorative, with the offscreen Learning Circle suggested by where the path leads.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera behaves like a curious path-level witness, sometimes just ahead of the characters, sometimes tucked near leaves that react to the poof. It does not obediently wait for entrances. Aida may be discovered through the trees as the camera notices disturbance before it fully finds her. With Bo’s questions, the camera stops being curious and becomes respectfully present.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: The scene’s movement belongs to the forest’s small reactions and the characters’ level changes. Poofs ripple the environment; Aida’s descent has comic physical imperfection; then everyone lowers into a shared stillness. Stillness is not absence of action — it is the moment the path stops demanding and the characters let Bo be where he is.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Depth carries story. The path ahead is the visible future; the seated trio is the present; the tail in open view is the past embarrassment transformed but not erased. Trees are not background wallpaper: they create Aida’s comic humility, carry wind after the final answer, and make the Learning Circle feel near enough to matter without showing it.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: The rhythm begins as playful cause-and-effect: countdown produces poof, poof tickles the forest, Bo giggles. The escalation is the growing awareness that the game is happening on a road to somewhere. Bo’s worry slows the tempo. Aida’s arrival adds a comic bump, then the scene narrows into four plain exchanges: scared too, every time, still go, every time. The second repetition lands as the scene’s quiet peak.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cut only when the forest gives us new information or the emotional relationship to the path changes. Early punctuation can ride environmental reactions rather than automatic faces. Once Bo names the worry, avoid cutting away just because someone has finished speaking; let pauses prove that no one is rushing him. The final hold is motivated by changed understanding, not sentimentality.
treatments.openingImage: A low view of the forest path with sunlight broken across it; a soft POOF drifts into the path’s air as Keen and Bo’s countdown game turns the route forward into a little stage.
treatments.closingImage: The same path stretches onward, but now Bo, Keen and Aida sit beside it in shared quiet. The wind moves through the trees after Aida’s answer, and Bo’s tail remains visible within the group rather than hidden from it.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: I want to resist the easy instinct to make the path a pretty backdrop behind medium character work. The path is the antagonist-pressure here — gentle, but real. We should compose depth so a young child always understands where forward is, while refusing fixed screen sides or a safe master that explains the geography without making us feel it.

treatments.name: No One Arrives Perfect
treatments.audienceExperience: The scene feels like a comic dismantling of perfect readiness. First Bo seems to have conquered the tail by making it perform. Then he admits he is not ready for the Learning Circle. Then Aida, the trusted elder, arrives visibly not polished by the forest. The audience laughs because everyone’s body gives them away, then relaxes because being given away does not disqualify anyone from belonging.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: This version shares the emotional lens between Bo and Aida’s example. Bo owns the fear; Aida reframes it not by explaining, but by embodying a confident person who still has traces of the hard climb on her. Keen is the bridge between them: he turns embarrassment into play, then introduces belonging without ceremony.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Primary comic mechanism: status change. Bo’s tail changes status from embarrassing accident to party trick; Aida changes status from distant elder to someone who has just lost a small battle with trees. The dramatic mechanism is parallel vulnerability: Bo’s tail and Aida’s twigs are both visible signs that no one arrives untouched.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Bo’s early performance is proud but fragile — he enjoys control, yet checks whether the fun is working on Keen. When the Learning Circle comes back into his mind, his attention drops from the game to the imagined group ahead. Keen’s performance must avoid fixing; he is quick in play and gentle in the pause, sitting beside Bo as an invitation, not a tactic. Aida carries authority through ease with imperfection: she does not fuss over the twigs or leaf, and that refusal to hide them gives Bo permission not to hide either. Her “I would have done five.” should feel like sincere comic solidarity, not a joke at Bo’s expense.
treatments.visualGrammar: The visual grammar uses visible imperfections as anchors. The poof is not cleaned up into a magical sparkle show; it is soft, funny, physical. Aida’s twigs and leaf are allowed to stay present. The scene favors frames where the thing a character might want to hide remains readable while the relationship continues around it.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera is affectionate but unsparing about little betrayals of the body. It notices the tail poof, notices Bo’s giggle, notices the worry return, notices Aida’s forest evidence. It does not shame any of it. The camera’s moral stance is: we look warmly at what you think you need to conceal, and we do not turn away.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Early movement is demonstrative: Bo making the poof happen, Keen counting, the game’s little rebounds. Aida’s entrance brings a different movement quality — slow, grounded, but with comic evidence of a rough descent. The stillness after she sits beside Bo is the answer: nobody needs to tidy themselves before being included.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: The ridge and trees create Aida’s imperfect arrival, while the path creates Bo’s imperfect readiness. Depth should connect those ideas: Aida comes from above or behind the tree line carrying proof of friction; Bo sits closer to the path carrying proof of worry. The forest becomes a place where every body picks up evidence of the journey.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: The rhythm escalates through three reveals. Reveal one: Bo can trigger the poof and laugh at it. Reveal two: the Learning Circle worry was still underneath the game. Reveal three: Aida, the steady one, also arrives marked by effort and admits fear plainly. Each reveal should get quieter than the previous one, so the emotional weight increases as the performance size decreases.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts should protect reveals rather than cover dialogue. The tail’s repeated poof needs comic punctuation, but not identical framing each time; each repetition should feel like Bo gaining temporary ownership. Bo’s worry earns a cut or reframing because the scene’s truth changes. Aida’s entrance earns discovery, not announcement. The last exchange should simplify editorially until the second “Every single time. BEAT.” has nowhere to hide.
treatments.openingImage: Bo’s tail doing “The Thing” again on command as Keen’s countdown turns the forest path into a tiny arena of success; Bo’s giggle tells us he is briefly winning against embarrassment.
treatments.closingImage: Aida sits with her forest-touched imperfection still visible, Keen beside Bo, Bo’s tail still present. The group is not polished, not moving yet, and not alone; the path waits in soft daylight.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: The danger is over-prettifying the elder entrance and accidentally making Aida’s confidence look flawless. I challenge us to frame her warmth and authority with the twigs and leaf clearly part of the image. If we hide the mess for elegance, we lose the scene’s argument: courage is not arriving perfect.

treatmentSelection.selectedTreatment: Countdown That Runs Out of Road — with the path-pressure of The Path Watches Back and the visible-imperfection rule of No One Arrives Perfect
combinedFrom: Countdown That Runs Out of Road
treatmentSelection.governingAudienceExperience: A giggly repeat-game slowly runs out of bounce, so the audience feels the exact moment Bo’s laugh becomes a held breath — then relaxes into quiet courage because no one rushes him, fixes him, or asks him to hide the tail.
treatmentSelection.rationale:
Use Countdown That Runs Out of Road as the spine. It has the cleanest emotional ownership: Bo’s tail moves from embarrassment to trick to visible truth, and the scene’s rhythm is a true energy curve rather than a string of events. Its best idea is that the countdown does not merely create comedy; it becomes the form of Bo’s avoidance, then stops when the real fear returns.

Fold in The Path Watches Back as the environmental pressure, not as a replacement POV. The path must be felt as the gentle future waiting beyond the game, with trees and wind keeping the Learning Circle present offscreen. That gives the scene visual originality and stops it becoming a simple sit-and-talk comfort scene.

Fold in No One Arrives Perfect for Aida’s entrance principle. Aida must not appear polished or magically above the problem. Her twigs-and-leaf arrival is not a side gag; it is the embodied argument of the scene: steady people still arrive marked by the effort of getting there. That makes her “Every single time” earned, plain, and funny-warm instead of wise-elder instruction.

The selected approach commits to Bo as the emotional owner, Keen as play-then-presence, and Aida as humility made visible. The closing value is not solved confidence; it is Bo’s tail still out in the open while the path still waits.
treatmentSelection.rejectionChecks:
No treatment is rejected for depending on fixed character lanes, keeping all characters visible, habitual action/reaction coverage, safe camera placement, repeated close-up punctuation, mechanical shot counts, generic “cinematic” language, or merely illustrating the script.

However, the treatments are not equal:

• The Path Watches Back is not chosen as the sole treatment because its path-as-governing-POV risks pulling authorship away from Bo if over-applied. The path should pressure the scene, not become the protagonist.

• No One Arrives Perfect is not chosen as the sole treatment because sharing the emotional lens between Bo and Aida could dilute the locked emotional ownership. Aida’s imperfection is essential, but it must answer Bo’s fear rather than become a parallel scene about her.

• Countdown That Runs Out of Road is selected because it most clearly protects meaning over plot, carries the comedy-to-ache rhythm, and avoids safe dialogue coverage by demanding a visible grammar shift from popping play to seated listening.

orderedEvents.text: 24	Four times.

orderedEvents.speaker: Aida
orderedEvents.text: 25	I would have done five.
Bo looks at her. Bo feels comfort and smiles.

beats.whatChanges: Aida enters not as untouchable certainty but as steady warmth marked by the effort of arrival; Bo receives comfort first through her visible imperfection and dry humility.
beats.whoDrives: Aida drives the change by climbing down imperfectly, naming the trees plainly, then sitting with Bo’s level of the moment.
beats.audienceAnticipation: The audience anticipates wise help, but first gets twigs, a leaf, and a grounded little joke that makes Aida safe rather than grand.
beats.actionOrChoice: Aida arrives with twigs and a leaf, accepts the mess without fuss, acknowledges Bo’s packed bag, and meets his “Four times” with a warmer one-up of shared preparation.
beats.consequence: Her authority becomes approachable; Bo is not corrected for over-preparing, and Keen’s introduction becomes a bridge rather than pressure.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The bag exchange lets the audience breathe and laugh softly before Bo asks the smaller, more direct question he truly needs answered.

emotionContract.entryState: Exposed after admitting the worry, watching for whether the arriving elder will make the fear feel bigger or smaller.
emotionContract.pressure: Aida’s arrival could make the Learning Circle feel official and intimidating if she appears too polished.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: Bo stays present for the introduction and answers plainly about packing four times.
emotionContract.exitState: A little more open; he has evidence that steadiness can be imperfect and preparation is not shameful.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: He remains seated with his tail visible, answers Aida’s bag line, and does not retreat from the new arrival.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: Aida has lowered the room’s pressure without denying that the first step is hard.

comedyContract.mechanism: Status softening through visible imperfection: the steady elder arrives with twigs and a leaf before offering comfort.
comedyContract.setup: Bo’s fear makes Aida’s arrival feel like it might become a solemn elder moment.
comedyContract.expectation: Aida will arrive smoothly and provide polished reassurance.
comedyContract.disruption: She has clearly had to negotiate the ridge and trees, then says “Tricky trees.” with calm humility.
comedyContract.button: “I would have done five.” turns Bo’s over-packing into something Aida can warmly understand.
comedyContract.hold: Let the twig-and-leaf image and Bo’s “Four times” breathe before Aida’s button lands; the laugh should make room, not erase the worry.

beats.sourceScript: Bo asks whether Aida also has to go through hard first steps, and Aida answers with plain repetition. The wind through the trees holds the cost: even the confident one keeps choosing to go.

orderedEvents.speaker: Bo
orderedEvents.text: 26	You get scared too?

orderedEvents.speaker: Aida
orderedEvents.text: 27	Every single time.

orderedEvents.speaker: Bo
orderedEvents.text: 28	But you still go?

orderedEvents.speaker: Aida
orderedEvents.text: 29	Every single time. BEAT.
Wind moves gently through the trees.

beats.whatChanges: Fear stops being proof that Bo cannot go; Aida’s repeated answer makes fear something steady people carry while still choosing the path.
beats.whoDrives: Bo drives the emotional inquiry with two small direct questions; Aida drives the answer by repeating the truth without enlarging it into a lesson.
beats.audienceAnticipation: The audience leans in for whether Aida will explain away the fear; instead, the same plain answer lands twice, heavier the second time.
beats.actionOrChoice: Bo asks if Aida gets scared and if she still goes; Aida answers both with the same unhurried truth while the group remains seated beside the path.
beats.consequence: Bo gains quiet courage without solved confidence; his tail remains visible, the path still waits, and the trees hold the unfinished cost.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The scene hands over a warm but unfinished closing image: three characters sitting in shared stillness, Bo’s tail open to view, and the Learning Circle still ahead.

emotionContract.entryState: Curious and vulnerable, needing to know whether fear disqualifies him from going.
emotionContract.pressure: Aida is the steady one; if she says she is never scared, Bo’s worry may feel like proof he is different.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: Bo asks the smallest true questions instead of hiding behind the tail game or the bag preparation.
emotionContract.exitState: Quieter and braver, not fixed; he can imagine going while still scared.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: He stays in the seated cluster, listens through the repeated answer, keeps the tail visible, and turns attention toward the path rather than only toward the tail.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The worry remains, but it is now shared; the final stillness carries courage and cost together.

comedyContract.mechanism: None; the repeated phrase is structured for emotional weight, not a gag.
comedyContract.setup: Aida’s previous humility has made her safe enough for Bo to ask directly.
comedyContract.expectation: Aida might give a reassuring explanation or remove the fear.
comedyContract.disruption: She simply admits the fear remains “Every single time.” and pairs it with continuing to go.
comedyContract.button: The second “Every single time. BEAT.” lands as quiet courage rather than punchline.
comedyContract.hold: Hold after the final line so wind, leaves, Bo’s visible tail, and the path carry the meaning without added explanation.

stagePlan.purpose: Turn Bo’s exposed tail into a playable prize through Keen’s first countdown invitation.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Keen walks beside Bo and counts “3,2,1 …”, causing Bo to prepare, commit, and make the tail poof on command for the first time.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The same tail event that could embarrass Bo becomes funny because Keen treats it as a shared trick and Bo accepts the game.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Begin at forest-path height with the poof already taking over attention; the camera is close enough to be startled by the bloom, then recoils slightly with Bo’s body reset instead of cutting away.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Bo has reset from the first poof with a visible little lift of pride, and Keen’s countdown energy remains pointed toward another try.

stagePlan.purpose: Build accumulated bounce so the later emotional stop has something real to lose.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Bo and Keen repeat the countdown with two distinct resets: one poof catches Bo a half-beat early and makes him hop-recover, then the final mastered poof lands exactly on Bo’s own “3,2,1 … POOF! The tail does ‘The Thing’ again and again. Bo giggles.”
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: Repetition becomes ownership; Bo is no longer being surprised by the tail but timing it for the laugh.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Stay in the moving pocket of the game: let the tail, Bo’s recoil, Keen’s forward lean, and Bo’s giggle reset the rhythm, with a small internal cut only after the second reset to make the final mastered poof feel earned rather than continuous mush.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Bo stands openly with the tail readable and his body buoyant from the mastered poof, giggling instead of hiding.

stagePlan.purpose: Break the game rhythm and prove Keen’s support changes from play-leading to witnessing.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Bo suddenly stops, his smile fades, he sits on the fallen log and grips his satchel tightly while saying “18	I’m STILL worried about going to the to the Learning Circle.”; Keen lets his own forward momentum die, lowers onto the log beside him with space, and Bo stares down the path before saying “19	They all know each other. Beat. But I don’t know them, and they don't know me.”
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The missing next countdown becomes the held breath; the path returns as social pressure, and Keen’s physical lowering tells Bo he will not be dragged past the worry.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: The camera does not re-establish; it drops with Bo’s attention from bounce to log height, allowing the path to stretch beyond his eyeline while Keen enters the lower seated plane rather than occupying the old play-leader height.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Bo and Keen sit beside the path with a respectful gap between them; Bo’s satchel is tight in his paws, his tail remains visible, and the path ahead occupies the open space he is looking into.

internalShotPlan.landingImage: The poof clears enough to reveal Bo reset upright with a quick pleased lift, tail still out in the open.
internalShotPlan.cutReason: No cut before the first poof because the anticipation-to-bloom cause must be felt whole; the next view is motivated only after the repeated game needs escalation.

internalShotPlan.purpose: Give the repetition distinct comic behaviour and a mastered final poof.
internalShotPlan.framingAndCamera: A looser walking pocket at Bo’s level, camera pacing backward just ahead of the two so the path becomes a play lane; it jitters back a fraction on each poof and settles on each reset.
internalShotPlan.storyAction: Bo and Keen run the countdown again; Bo’s first repeat arrives slightly early with a hop-recover, then Bo times the final countdown himself and giggles through the mastered result.
internalShotPlan.performanceFocus: Bo’s timing grows from surprised participation to proud command; Keen stays alert to Bo’s delight rather than pushing the game bigger than Bo wants.
internalShotPlan.landingImage: Bo holds the final poof’s aftermath in open view, giggling, with Keen angled toward him in delighted readiness for another round.
internalShotPlan.cutReason: The internal cut sharpens the rhythm from first surprise into repeatable game; staying in the first view would make “again and again” feel like a blur instead of escalating behaviours.

internalShotPlan.purpose: Let the accumulated bounce visibly run out and center Keen’s costly adjustment beside Bo.
internalShotPlan.framingAndCamera: The frame slows and lowers as Bo stops; log, satchel, visible tail, and the forward path share the composition, with Keen entering by lowering into the frame rather than being cut to as a reaction.
internalShotPlan.storyAction: Bo sits and grips the satchel; he says the first worry line, Keen sits beside him with space, and Bo looks down the path before naming that the others know each other and he does not know them.
internalShotPlan.performanceFocus: Bo’s body loses spring before the words arrive; Keen’s choice is to let his own play-leader energy go quiet and physically join Bo’s level without crowding him.
internalShotPlan.landingImage: Two small seated figures at log height beside a path that continues beyond them; Bo’s satchel is clutched, his tail is visible, and Keen’s body is still beside him with room left between them.
internalShotPlan.cutReason: The emotional turn needs one held descent from movement into stillness; cutting to Keen’s reaction would weaken the proof that his support is behavioural, not verbal punctuation.

shots.purpose: Carry the full laugh-to-held-breath reversal: the tail becomes a repeatable trick Bo owns, then the Learning Circle worry stops the game and Keen proves care by lowering beside him.
shots.audienceExperience: The audience gets the childlike pleasure of “again!” through specific poof resets, then feels the exact absence of the next countdown when Bo’s attention is pulled down the path.
shots.openingImage: At forest-path height, Bo’s tail poof blooms in a sun patch just as Keen’s countdown motion leans into the frame beside him.
shots.principalPerformance: Bo begins buoyant and increasingly precise with the poof, then loses spring all at once when the path becomes the Learning Circle again; Keen changes from bright play instigator to quiet seated witness, leaving Bo space instead of urging him onward.
shots.cameraRelationship: Bo-adjacent and rhythm-sensitive: surprised by the first bloom, carried by the repeat game, then lowered into seated listening without retreating to a safe master.
shots.physicalOrEmotionalChange: Bo briefly retitles the tail from exposed problem to owned trick, then admits the trick has not removed the social fear; Keen’s posture changes the relationship from game-leading to being-with.
shots.closingImage: Bo and Keen sit on the fallen log with a careful gap between them. Bo’s satchel is held tight, his tail remains visible, and the path ahead stays open under the trees.
shots.transitionReason: A planned cut is stronger because Aida’s arrival is a new visual idea and a changed source of steadiness; remaining continuous from the seated two-shot would make her feel like coverage entering a dialogue triangle instead of a fresh interruption from Bo’s eyeline and the ridge.
shots.providerBoundaryExplanation: This unit’s honest game build, reversal, two worry lines, Keen’s physical lowering, and landing hold require about 27 seconds; adding Aida’s imperfect arrival, bag exchange, direct questions, repeated answers, wind, and final hold would exceed 30 seconds and overload the unit beyond three causal stages.

cinematographyContract.emotionalDistanceEnd: Close but less kinetic, seated near enough to feel Bo’s grip and Keen’s chosen stillness while the path presses in.

performanceBudget.rationale: The unit needs three distinct poof behaviours plus the full bodily drop into worry and Keen’s seated adjustment. It fits under 30 seconds with three stages and does not need a split before Aida because the split is stronger after Bo and Keen land in shared stillness.

storyIntent.narrativeFunction: Transform the tail from embarrassment into owned play, then expose that play cannot erase the fear of entering a group.
storyIntent.primaryAudienceFeeling: Giggly anticipation that becomes a small held breath.
storyIntent.secondaryAudienceFeeling: Relief that Keen notices the change and stops leading before support becomes pressure.
storyIntent.outerAction: Keen counts down; Bo triggers repeated tail poofs, stops, sits, grips his satchel, and names the Learning Circle worry while Keen sits beside him.
storyIntent.innerAction: Bo tries on control, enjoys it, then admits the worry underneath; Keen gives up being the fun engine so Bo can be witnessed.
storyIntent.performanceDirection: Bo’s poof timing should grow more intentional with each reset, then lose lift before the first worry line; Keen should visibly spend his own momentum by sitting, not hovering in readiness to move on.
storyIntent.mutedRead: With sound off, the audience understands: tail trick becomes fun through repetition; Bo stops and shrinks toward the log; Keen lowers beside him; the path ahead is what Bo is worried about.
storyIntent.environmentPressure: The path begins as a play lane under dapples, then becomes an open route toward offscreen others when Bo looks away from the tail.
storyIntent.soundStory: Countdown rhythm and soft poofs set the game; after Bo stops, the missing countdown, smaller breaths, and quieter forest bed deepen the drop without explaining it.
storyIntent.motifUse: The tail poof is first a prize and then remains visible as the worry returns; sitting beside begins as Keen’s proof of care.
storyIntent.thoughtChangeAndCut: The unit holds until Bo’s thought changes from “I can make this funny” to “I am still scared of them”; the cut comes only after Keen has met that thought by sitting with him.
storyIntent.mustUnderstand: Bo is not embarrassed in this safe pocket anymore, but he is still afraid of the Learning Circle; Keen responds by making room.
storyIntent.mustNotKnowYet: Aida’s answer that she also gets scared and still goes must not arrive in this unit.
storyIntent.reactionBeat: Keen’s meaning-changing reaction is physical: he stops being the countdown leader and sits beside Bo with space.
storyIntent.relationshipDistance: Playful walking closeness becomes seated closeness with a careful gap that respects Bo’s vulnerability.
storyIntent.relationshipPowerDynamic: Keen begins as the energetic game-maker, then gives up the lead so Bo’s worry can set the pace.
storyIntent.touchOrAvoidance: No touch; care is shown by proximity without crowding and by leaving the tail visible without pointing at it.
storyIntent.eyelineRule: During play, eyes track countdown and tail; at the turn, Bo’s eyeline must leave the game and find the path ahead before the deeper worry line.
storyIntent.silhouetteRead: Bo’s lifted, springy outline collapses into a small seated shape; Keen’s taller forward energy lowers into a matching still shape beside him.
storyIntent.silenceRule: Protect the silence after Bo stops and before Keen fully settles; the absence of the next countdown is the turn.
storyIntent.scoreInstruction: Withhold score under the game or keep it as light rhythmic punctuation; thin it out when Bo stops so forest quiet and breath carry the worry.

shots.physicalPerformance: Bo’s tail blooms become a playable rhythm: brace, burst, recoil, reset, with each reset more proudly held in the open. When the path pressure returns, his spring drains before he sits and locks onto the satchel. Keen spends his forward energy visibly, lowering beside Bo with a careful gap instead of urging him onward.
shots.animationTiming: Start with buoyant repeat beats and distinct recoil-resets, allowing each tail bloom to land before the next invitation. The turn is the missing next play beat: motion thins, Bo’s sit has weight, and Keen’s lowering is unhurried enough to read as chosen care.

performanceContract.playableIntention: Bo tries to make the exposed tail belong to him, then admits the game has not carried him past the fear ahead. Keen first makes safety through play, then makes safety by staying low beside him.

phases.observableAction: Keen walks angled toward Bo with bright forward lean, marking a playful cue with shoulders, paws, and body rhythm while leaving Bo room to choose the tail response.
Bo braces, releases the tail into repeated soft blooms, recoils or hop-recovers from each burst, then resets more upright and open with the tail still visible.
After the mastered burst, Bo’s lift drains; his paws close hard around the satchel, his body folds down onto the fallen log, and his eyes leave the tail for the path ahead.
Keen lets his forward lean die, lowers onto the log beside Bo with a visible gap, quiets his paws, and aims his body toward Bo and the path rather than onward.

performanceContract.physicalCauseAndEffect: Keen’s rhythmic invitation gives Bo a predictable cue, letting Bo prepare the tail bloom instead of being ambushed by it. Each bloom pushes Bo into a small physical recoil that proves the burst has weight, and each reset gives him a clearer hold on the trick. When Bo’s attention catches on the path, the repeating rhythm stops; his seated weight and satchel grip end the game, and Keen’s matching descent changes the space from play lane to listening place.
performanceContract.visibleEmotionalTurn: Bo changes from springy ownership of the tail to a smaller seated shape that keeps the tail visible while the worry takes over. Keen changes from moving game-maker to still witness.
performanceContract.requiredLanding: Bo and Keen sit on the fallen log beside the open path with a respectful gap between them; Bo’s satchel is tight in his paws, his tail remains visible, and the route ahead holds the pressure in the frame.
performanceContract.performanceFreedom: Animators may vary Bo’s micro-recoils, giggle-shakes, ear and fur follow-through, and Keen’s exact paw rhythm, but the shot must preserve distinct tail-bloom resets, the hard absence of the next play cue, Bo’s weighted sit, and Keen’s non-crowding gap.

shots.purpose: Answer Bo’s worry with Aida’s imperfect arrival, shared preparation, and plain courage while keeping the Learning Circle present as the path beyond them.
shots.audienceExperience: The audience laughs softly at Aida arriving with twigs and a leaf, then leans into the repeated answers and settles into courage that remains unfinished.
shots.openingImage: From Bo’s seated eyeline, leaves stir on the ridge above the path as Aida begins climbing down through them.

storyIntent.narrativeFunction: Introduce Aida as imperfectly steady and let her plain repeated truth give Bo a way to carry fear forward.
storyIntent.primaryAudienceFeeling: Soft laughter turning into attentive quiet.
storyIntent.secondaryAudienceFeeling: Warm relief that no one makes Bo’s fear smaller than it is.
storyIntent.outerAction: Aida descends from the ridge, brushes off twigs, sits beside Bo, recognizes his packed bag, answers his direct questions, and the wind moves through the trees.
storyIntent.innerAction: Bo tests whether Aida is safe, accepts her recognition, then asks if fear disqualifies him; he hears that fear can remain while one still goes.
storyIntent.performanceDirection: Aida should underplay the wisdom and make the descent’s mess ordinary; Bo should not brighten into solved confidence, only ease enough to keep listening with the tail in view.
storyIntent.mutedRead: With sound off, Aida’s twig-and-leaf arrival lowers her status, her spaced sitting lowers pressure, the satchel exchange comforts Bo, and the final still cluster with moving leaves shows courage without resolution.
storyIntent.environmentPressure: The ridge and trees make Aida’s arrival imperfect; the path remains in Bo’s body angle and background depth so the offscreen Learning Circle keeps tugging even during comfort.
storyIntent.soundStory: Leaf rustle announces Aida before dialogue; the bag exchange has room for a small laugh; the final answers sit over reduced forest sound until wind through leaves carries the last beat.
storyIntent.motifUse: The tail is no longer asked to perform and remains openly visible; sitting beside expands from Keen’s care to Aida’s care; the path stays as the gentle demand.
storyIntent.thoughtChangeAndCut: Bo’s thought changes from “Will this steady person judge my worry?” to “Even she is scared and still goes”; the scene holds until wind and the visible tail let that thought settle.
storyIntent.mustUnderstand: Aida does not erase fear; she admits it and still chooses the path, giving Bo quiet courage.
storyIntent.mustNotKnowYet: Whether Bo will succeed at the Learning Circle is not answered here.
storyIntent.reactionBeat: Bo’s comforted look after Aida’s bag line changes the meaning of her arrival from official help to safe company.
storyIntent.relationshipDistance: Aida sits close enough to be with Bo but leaves a visible gap; Keen remains nearby without reclaiming leadership.
storyIntent.relationshipPowerDynamic: Aida’s elder authority is softened by her imperfect descent and by matching Bo’s preparation rather than correcting it.
storyIntent.touchOrAvoidance: No touch is required; care is shown through sitting, spacing, and shared orientation toward the path.
storyIntent.eyelineRule: Bo looks up to discover Aida, down or to the satchel during the preparation exchange, then between Aida and the path as his questions test whether going is possible.
storyIntent.silhouetteRead: Aida’s descent is slightly irregular, then grounded; Bo’s seated shape stays small but less clenched; the final cluster reads as three still bodies beside a continuing route.
storyIntent.silenceRule: Protect the beat after Aida’s final answer and the wind through the trees; do not fill it with movement, reassurance, or extra business.
storyIntent.scoreInstruction: Let score stay withheld or barely present under Aida’s arrival; if it enters, it should be sparse and sustained after the second answer, leaving wind and breath audible.

shots.physicalPerformance: Aida arrives with grounded control but imperfect contact with the ridge: small balance checks, twig brushing, and the leaf left caught long enough to soften her authority. shots.animationTiming: Aida’s descent has gentle irregularity and a small comic hold on the remaining leaf before the seated exchange settles. Let the bag recognition breathe, then slow into longer still answers, with the final leaf movement held after bodies go quiet.

performanceContract.playableIntention: Bo tests whether the steady elder is safe to trust and whether fear disqualifies him. Aida answers by making her steadiness plain, imperfect, and unforced; Keen remains present without taking the lead back.

phases.observableAction: Leaves above Bo stir in uneven rustles, and ridge foliage parts before Aida is fully visible.

performanceContract.physicalCauseAndEffect: The ridge and branches make Aida’s arrival visibly effortful, so her authority is softened before she sits. Her choice to leave space prevents the new closeness from crowding Bo. Her attention to the satchel redirects Bo’s preparation from shame to recognition, causing his grip to ease. The final wind carries the unresolved path forward after the characters stop moving.
performanceContract.visibleEmotionalTurn: Bo shifts from guarded watchfulness to quiet courage: not brighter or fixed, but less clenched and able to keep looking between Aida and the route ahead. Aida’s elder steadiness becomes approachable because the trees have visibly scuffed it first.
performanceContract.requiredLanding: Bo, Keen, and Aida sit in a quiet cluster beside the path; Bo’s tail remains openly visible, the satchel is no longer crushed as tightly, and moving leaves over the route show the next step still waiting.

scene.dramaticQuestion: Can Bo let his tail stay visible and still face the path toward bears who do not know him yet?
scene.connectionFromPreviousScene: Bo arrives with the tail still carrying the meaning of “The Thing”; Keen meets that exposure with play instead of correction.
scene.handoverToNextScene: Bo is not magically confident, but he is less alone: he remains beside Keen and Aida with the tail in the open while the path toward the Learning Circle continues ahead.

beats.sourceScript: On the forest path, Keen turns Bo’s tail into a countdown game. Bo makes the poof happen on purpose again and again, briefly changing the tail from a problem into a trick he owns.
exactDialogue: Bo: 3,2,1 … POOF! The tail does ‘The Thing’ again and again. Bo giggles.

orderedEvents.text: A winding path through the Whispering Woods. Sunlight flickers through the leaves. Bo walks beside Keen. Step. Step. Keen counts down.
BO makes his tail do ‘The Thing’ on command. POOF!
BO/KEEN 3, 2, 1 …
POOF! The tail does ‘The Thing’ again and again.

orderedEvents.text: 3,2,1 … POOF! The tail does ‘The Thing’ again and again. Bo giggles.

dialogueOccurrences.speaker: Bo
dialogueOccurrences.exactText: 3,2,1 … POOF! The tail does ‘The Thing’ again and again. Bo giggles.

beats.whatChanges: Bo’s tail is temporarily re-titled from exposed problem to repeatable trick; the forest path becomes a play lane instead of only the route toward the Learning Circle.
beats.whoDrives: Keen drives the support by turning the tail into a game; Bo completes the change by joining the countdown and making the poof happen on purpose.
beats.audienceAnticipation: The audience waits for the next “POOF!” like a child asking for the trick again, enjoying the tiny suspense of whether Bo can make it happen when invited.
beats.actionOrChoice: Keen offers the countdown rhythm; Bo accepts it, repeats it, and lets the tail perform in the open instead of trying to hide it.
beats.consequence: The poof keeps paying off, Bo giggles, and the tail briefly belongs to him as a funny invention rather than an embarrassment.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The repeated laugh creates ownership, but the rhythm is now available to run out when the path and the Learning Circle press back in.

emotionContract.entryState: Playful relief with worry underneath; he wants the tail to become something he can control.
emotionContract.pressure: The tail has been the thing that gives him away, and the path still leads toward others offscreen.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: He chooses to play with the poof on command instead of shrinking from it.
emotionContract.exitState: Briefly proud and delighted, with the deeper Learning Circle worry still waiting beyond the game.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: He joins the countdown, lets the tail poof visibly again and again, and giggles rather than tucking it away.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The tail can be funny in this safe pocket, but the route forward has not disappeared.

comedyContract.mechanism: Repetition with emotional reversal: the same tail event that embarrassed Bo becomes a prize the game can trigger again.
comedyContract.setup: Keen’s countdown prepares the audience for the tail’s response.
comedyContract.expectation: The tail will do “The Thing” once as a joke and Bo will be embarrassed by it.
comedyContract.disruption: Bo can make it happen again and again, turning the embarrassing poof into a trick he owns.
comedyContract.button: Bo’s own line and giggle confirm that he is now playing the poof rather than being betrayed by it.
comedyContract.hold: Let each poof land long enough for Bo’s delight to register before the next countdown restarts the rhythm.

physicalStaging.staysVisible: Bo’s tail remains readable before, during, and after each poof so the audience tracks cause, burst, and recovery without losing Bo’s reaction.
physicalStaging.contactAndWeight: The poof has soft body consequence: Bo’s small recoil and reset prove the burst affects him, while Keen’s forward countdown energy stays light and inviting rather than pushy.
physicalStaging.payoffShape: A repeating countdown-to-bloom shape: anticipation gathers, the tail blooms, Bo recoils or perks, then the giggle resets the game.
prohibitedStaging: Do not cut away from the tail at the instant of payoff.
Do not make the poof feel like a magical power-up or solved confidence.
Do not let Keen’s energy shove Bo physically toward the Learning Circle.

beats.sourceScript: The game stops when Bo remembers the Learning Circle is not just an idea; it is other people who already know each other. Keen sits beside him and gives him space instead of pulling him on.

Bo: 19	They all know each other. Beat. But I don’t know them, and they don't know me.
